Current coordinated release status — October 20, 2026

The current local candidates are ForgeMCP core 0.3.14, Unreal plugin 0.2.14-alpha.3, and Blender add-on 0.2.36-alpha.1. Their packages passed the bounded core, Blender clean-profile, and disposable isolated Unreal tests described in the release record [not indexed]. The Unreal Editor target compiled, while the full UAT BuildPlugin pipeline remains blocked by the installed engine's missing BuildSettings.precompiled manifest. The Unreal acceptance used -NullRHI and a small non-World-Partition level. Neither existing Editor was updated; Phase 6C remains NO-GO.

The native dirty-package observer enumerates loaded UPackage objects, but the disposable acceptance surfaced one dirty /Script/SlateCore row with incomplete classification and truncated associated objects. Treat unresolved rows as a preservation blocker. This feature does not prove that all in-memory state is captured or that restart is safe.

The original roadmap and prior dated status below remain historical evidence.

Roadmap implementation status — October 16, 2026

The full user goal remains active. The original roadmap is preserved as supplied. The MCP server source is version 0.3.13, the engine-installed Unreal plugin is 0.2.13-alpha.9, and the latest Blender add-on is 0.2.35-alpha.6 (Blender numeric metadata 0.2.35). Component versions advance with validated component changes. Coordinated v1.0.0 remains gated on completing the roadmap's installation, live-session, capability, recovery and packaging criteria; these development versions are not completion of universal Unreal/Blender control.

The alpha.9 Unreal tab white-screen fix is installed engine-wide. Its single-file React bundle passed Chromium runtime and isolated UE 5.6.1 package checks; the standard desktop Unreal WebBrowser still needs a visual refresh check. See white-tab fix evidence and the official partner logo integration record. The current reference-matched spacing and icon refinement is documented in the compact layout note.

October 16 — Automatic dual-application session check

Server 0.3.11 adds forge_ensure_connected. Each call rediscovers registered sessions, authenticates each app with a health request and returns a session ID only when exactly one live bridge exists for that app. Optional explicit IDs resolve multiple live sessions without guessing. This verifies connectivity with short requests; it does not retain sockets or launch bridges. Unit and stdio MCP tests cover automatic selection, explicit selection, ambiguity, missing bridges and registration discovery. In the current environment Blender blender-5048 responds as 0.2.35-alpha.4; no Unreal bridge is responding, although an UnrealEditor process exists. Unreal connection remains pending its bridge startup.

October 16 — Blender add-on alpha.4 alignment

Blender add-on 0.2.35-alpha.4 aligns its release label with the Unreal alpha.4 milestone. Its Send to Unreal Asset path now defaults to /Game/Content/Returns/; the existing transfer flow appends the exact Blender source object name. Blender's numeric bl_info version remains (0, 2, 35); the package filename and authenticated bridge health expose the full prerelease label. The 10-module ZIP (Artifacts/ForgeMCP-Blender-Addon-0.2.35-alpha.4.zip, SHA-256 ca052fdbd6f18dc9d93e2c429140886d35d3ed1dfcc4b83f5577f7d6459b5a9f) passed the Blender 5.2.2 clean-profile install, enable/disable, cached-module reload and existing native acceptance checks. The user Blender 5.2 add-on source was updated with per-file backups. Blender was running during installation, so its already-loaded adapter still needs an add-on reload or Blender restart before the live bridge reports the new version. No scene data or preferences were changed.

October 16 — Blender tab redesign, alpha.5

The Blender 3D Viewport ForgeMCP sidebar now follows the supplied reference with a branded version card, grouped Bridge Status and Send to Unreal panels, clear connection/session timing, and aligned transfer settings. The transfer still uses the existing reviewed preview/confirm flow and /Game/Content/Returns/ default. The source and package report 0.2.35-alpha.5; Blender's numeric add-on metadata remains (0, 2, 35). Blender 5.2.2 headless draw and clean-profile package checks passed, the add-on was installed in the 5.2 user folder, and a fresh process registered the installed source. Interactive sidebar rendering in a live Blender window remains a separate visual check. See alpha.5 Blender UI acceptance [not indexed].

October 16 — Blender reference-match refinement, alpha.6

The alpha.5 layout was too generic compared with the supplied image. Alpha.6 centers the large logo above the product name/version, enlarges the bridge action, removes the duplicate transfer heading, and presents placement coordinates as separate X/Y/Z rows. The installed alpha.5 process is still running; alpha.6 source and package validation plus installation are tracked in alpha.6 visual refinement.

October 16 — Alpha.2 engine-mesh panel transfer fix

Installed alpha.2 and server source 0.3.7 fix the selected engine sphere's rejected source path and the async exception masking behind panel_worker_failed. Python tests (339), lint, the module-restricted editor build, native source-preservation automation and real FBX/OBJ panel-worker transfers into disposable Blender passed. The updated engine DLL passed fresh-project load and real stdio MCP inspection. Native source stays in the engine installation at the user's request. See alpha.2 evidence.

October 16 — Alpha.3 Blender handoff and import preflight UX

The import message identified an existing destination only as destination_exists. The live project already contains /Game/ForgeMCP/Returns/SM_Return, so the guard was correct; the panel now explains how to choose a new path or use an eligible bound replacement. The Send to Blender object-name field now starts blank and keeps the source mesh asset name unless the user enters an override. The isolated 27-action native build, engine update, fresh engine-wide plugin load, and live ForgeMCPDev bridge check passed. Visual panel confirmation remains unverified. See alpha.3 evidence.

October 16 — Transfer name preservation and Unreal return folder

Server 0.3.10 and Unreal alpha.4 use /Game/Content/Returns/ as the Blender-to- Unreal destination folder and retain the exact source object name as the new mesh asset name. No prefix, suffix, or collision-driven rename is generated; an existing exact destination remains a preflight error. Unreal-to-Blender continues to default to the source Unreal asset name, with a blank optional override. Alpha.4 source is in the engine installation. Build, package and engine-wide load evidence is recorded in transfer name acceptance; interactive two-application transfer verification remains open until both bridges are connected.

October 16 — UE 5.6.1 engine-wide alpha

Plugin 0.2.13-alpha.1 was packaged and installed engine-wide for UE 5.6.1 Win64 Development Editor. Python regression tests (335), lint, native module builds and the full isolated editor target passed. A fresh Blueprint-only project without a local plugin copy loaded the engine DLL, matched the package bytes/version, and passed authenticated inspection plus real source stdio MCP discovery and project identity checks. Visible UI, all-feature and performance acceptance remain open. See alpha evidence [not indexed] and installation/update/rollback. Feature development continues in the separate project-local plugin; the v1.0 roadmap remains active.

Current progress estimate — 2026-10-11

These are engineering estimates against roadmap breadth, integration, failure recovery and release readiness, not a count of command names. The coordinated v1.0.0 goal is approximately 55% complete. Unreal automation is approximately 58%, Blender automation 62%, bidirectional file transfer 60%, and clean installation/live integration/recovery 42%. Estimates reflect tested workflows as well as gaps; real-time synchronization is not implemented.

Currently practical: typed, reviewed MCP operations can inspect and edit supported Unreal actors, assets, Blueprints, materials, levels and DataAssets; inspect Blender objects, meshes, materials, rigs and animation; perform several reviewed Blender mesh/material/node/modifier edits; and transfer static mesh FBX/OBJ assets between Unreal and Blender with bindings and revision checks. Python is used by the server and Blender adapter, but arbitrary user-supplied Unreal Python execution is not an approved remote operation. C++ plugin changes can be made in source and packaged; compilation can be triggered locally, though a complete editor-target build and live editor activation remain unverified for this increment.

Still outside reliable coverage: arbitrary Blueprint graph authoring, UMG, broad World Partition/PCG/Niagara workflows, Unreal skeletal/animation pipelines, Blender rig/weight editing and broad destructive graph edits, durable cross-operation recovery, real-time two-way synchronization, and universal clean-install activation.
